newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. calls for action to deter Israeli settlements.
newsitem.headline: U.N. calls for action to deter Israeli settlements.

text.p: The General Assembly recommended on Tuesday that U.N. members "actively discourage" activities that contribute to Israeli settlement-building in occupied territories and demanded that Israel provide information about goods produced or manufactured in the settlements.
The vote on the resolution, at a resumed emergency special session of the Assembly, was 131 to three, with 14 abstentions.
The draft, hinting at sanctions that only the Security Council can impose, was softened compared with an earlier version to attract maximum support.

It condemns Israel's failure to comply with a resolution adopted in April by 134 to three, with 11 abstentions, demanding that it cease construction of 6,500 homes at a site south of Jerusalem captured in the 1967 Middle East war called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.

The new resolution also recommends that the parties to the Fourth Geneva Convention, which bars settlements in occupied territory, hold a conference on measures to enforce the convention and asks the U.N. secretary-general to provide a report in three months.

Speaking shortly before the vote, United States U.N. representative Bill Richardson called the draft "a partisan resolution aimed not at building confidence or dialogue, but at confrontation" and said he would vote against it.
